clue.text: When my speech is written, they should mark my words

definitions.text: When my speech is written, they should mark my words

parts.words: When my speech is written, they should mark my words
parts.note: quotation marks are what a writer puts round someone's spoken words when setting them down on the page

explanation.surface: A speaker insisting that anyone writing up their speech had better record it faithfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark my words' sounds like a warning to take heed, but it is literal: these punctuation marks enclose quoted words.
explanation.definitionFit: Quotation marks, the British name, surround reported speech when it is written down.

clue.text: Material from US city underwritten by 50% of capital

indicators.note: in a down clue, being written underneath means the second piece comes below the first

parts.note: NY is the usual abbreviation for New York

indicators.note: half of the six-letter capital city is taken, its opening three letters

parts.note: London is the capital of the UK

explanation.surface: Fabric sourced from an American city, with the deal underwritten by half the money from investors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money backing a deal; here it is the capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic fibre and the fabric woven from it, so it is a material.

clue.text: Appoint this person that's come up with scheme

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the setter referring to themself gives ME
a ploy is a cunning plan or scheme

explanation.surface: An appointment made of someone who has arrived bearing a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person' is the setter speaking of themself, a standard crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To hire or take someone on for a job, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Smashed particle — it becomes more than double

indicators.note: something smashed is broken into pieces, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A particle accelerator image: a smashed particle splits into more pieces than two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashed' rearranges PARTICLE plus IT; the definition is a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to treble is to multiply threefold, which is more than doubling.

clue.text: Wild animal or something at the water's edge, looking up

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: reeds are tall grasses growing along the banks of rivers and ponds

explanation.surface: Spotting either a wild creature or a plant on the shoreline when glancing upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag or doe is a wild animal of the forest and park.

clue.text: Motorway exit where tractors should go?

definitions.meaning: leaving the motorway means getting away from the main road altogether
farm vehicles are built to drive across fields rather than along tarmac

explanation.surface: A grumbling driver stuck behind farm traffic on a motorway slip road.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes driving across rough country away from paved highways.

clue.text: Looks painful, having ring inserted in facial feature

indicators.note: the ring is placed inside the other phrase's letters

parts.note: something that looks painful must ache, read as two words
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A face piercing that looks sore, with a ring pushed through the lip area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looks painful' is MUST ACHE run together; O goes in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair grown on the upper lip is a feature of some faces.

clue.text: Weekly magazine's laid on wine for Wimbledon tennis perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece laid on top of another comes first

parts.note: The Spectator is a British weekly political magazine; the 's adds S
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A magazine hosting a wine reception for the Wimbledon crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spectator is a long-running British weekly magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Wimbledon tennis is an example of a game watched by large crowds, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Pictures, strangely shiny, set in process that gives everything more life

definitions.text: process that gives everything more life

parts.note: photos are pictures taken with a camera

indicators.note: something done strangely is out of its usual order, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Odd shiny photographs set into some vague life-giving procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' rearranges SHINY and SET together to give YNTHESIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants convert sunlight into food by this reaction, sustaining nearly all life on Earth.

clue.text: Charlie dances about following parking for reduced rate

indicators.note: the rearranged name goes around the two abbreviations
the name dances about, so its letters move into a new order

parts.note: F is the usual abbreviation for following, as in page references
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie dancing round a car park for a cheap ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like a position word for the charade, but it is the abbreviation F, enclosed along with P.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling at half the usual cost is a cut or discounted price.

clue.text: Fine old instrument used to make glass

parts.note: F is short for fine, as on pencil leads
the lute is a plucked string instrument of medieval and Renaissance times

explanation.surface: A fine antique instrument repurposed in glassmaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' tempts as the definition, but the woodwind is a red herring: the definition is the champagne glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall narrow wine glass, typically for champagne, carries this name.

clue.text: Labour carrying in loud chef's essential item?

indicators.note: the work-word carries the other letters inside it

parts.note: toil is hard work or labour
F stands for forte, the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A loud kitchen where the chef's hard work involves one indispensable tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the political party, but it is just hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Aluminium wrapping is a kitchen staple for covering and roasting, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Note that one may leave quickly after hanky-panky

definitions.text: Note that one may leave quickly after hanky-panky

parts.words: Note that one may leave quickly after hanky-panky
parts.note: a sticky memo slip is the kind of hasty message someone might stick up when slipping away after a fling

explanation.surface: A lover dashing off after a tryst, leaving only a hurried note behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sticky-backed paper note, left on a fridge or mirror.

clue.text: Nuts attached to bonnet maybe limiting force in part of engine

indicators.note: the first piece is joined directly onto the second

parts.note: cranks are eccentrics, people one might call nuts

indicators.note: the headgear word hems in the force letter

parts.note: a bonnet is an example of a hat
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A mechanic attaching nuts under a car bonnet near the engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bonnet' looks like the car's hood but is headwear; 'limiting' puts F inside HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating shaft that turns piston motion into rotation is a component of an engine.

clue.text: Boyhood's occasionally misplaced, coming from east London area

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading from right to left
every other letter of the word is lost, keeping only alternate ones

explanation.surface: A man's childhood lost now and then, having come from the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East London' looks like one phrase; 'east' belongs to the reversal, and SOHO is in the West End.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of central London known for nightlife, theatres and restaurants.

clue.text: Masses hit oil pool with no time to deviate

indicators.note: the letters deviate from their order, so they are rearranged
the time letter is taken out of the first word

explanation.surface: A crowd striking an oil reservoir and having no time to change course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no' removes T from HIT; 'to deviate' rearranges HI, OIL and POOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek for 'the many', used in English for ordinary people or the common crowd.

clue.text: Vacant sty pens worried pet chicken

indicators.note: the emptied word pens in, or encloses, the other piece
with the middle emptied, only the outside letters of the word stay

parts.note: to have cared is to have fretted or worried
a cat is a common household pet

explanation.surface: A pig's empty sty holding an anxious pet hen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' looks like the poultry in the sty but means a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is informal for a coward, a timid person easily frightened.

clue.text: Tense and bitter after arrest

indicators.note: the bitter-word comes after the arrest-word

parts.note: to nail someone is to catch or arrest them
a bitter wind is a biting one

explanation.surface: A suspect anxious and resentful after being taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like grammar but is an adjective meaning anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a nerve-racking situation that keeps one on edge, fretting with suspense.

clue.text: British getting over defeat order something pink and frothy?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another comes first

parts.note: a loss is a defeat
the OM, Order of Merit, is a British order of honour

explanation.surface: A Briton recovering from defeat with a pink, fluffy cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting over' looks like recovering, but just places B above LOSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherry and apple flowers are pink, frothy masses on the branch, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Amber nectar insect's found by river

indicators.note: the river letter is found beside, after, the insect

parts.note: a bee is an insect; the 's is a link
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A bee collecting amber nectar beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nectar' suggests bees, but 'amber nectar' is slang for lager.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber nectar is a jocular phrase, made famous by an Australian lager advert, for the alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Lots of squares taking in arrangements of basic numbers — it's puzzling

definitions.text: Lots of squares taking in arrangements of basic numbers — it's puzzling

parts.words: Lots of squares taking in arrangements of basic numbers — it's puzzling
parts.note: a grid of eighty-one cells to be filled with the digits one to nine in a logical arrangement

explanation.surface: A bewildered description of conventional types absorbing simple arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squares' tempts as dull conventional people; here they are the cells of a grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese number-placement puzzle on a nine-by-nine grid.

clue.text: Loves wearing different red suits, plus spectacles for a spell

indicators.note: the red-suit letters wear the loves inside them

parts.note: the two red suits in cards are hearts and diamonds, H and D
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O, so two loves give OO
a pair of spectacles looks like two Os

explanation.surface: Loves dressed in red, wearing glasses, under some enchantment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spectacles' gives OO by shape, like the lenses of glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: A hex or curse, a bad-luck charm in voodoo tradition.

clue.text: A portrait may be this high and mighty

definitions.meaning: a picture is fixed or pinned up on a wall
arrogant and snooty, looking down on others

explanation.surface: A portrait of a lofty, haughty aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally fixed aloft on a wall, figuratively snobbish and conceited.

clue.text: In Moscow, change on the rise awoke poker-faced guards

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from the bottom upwards
the phrase guards the letters inside it

explanation.surface: A Muscovite waking up stony-faced, as guards stand at attention amid change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guards' looks like a noun but is the verb that hides KEPOK, which 'on the rise' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian coin worth a hundredth of a rouble, small change in Moscow.

clue.text: Frank in love with writer

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a pen is something that writes

explanation.surface: A man named Frank who has fallen for an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid and honest, holding nothing back.

clue.text: Article should be wrapped in less plastic, in which 10 items could go

indicators.note: the article goes inside the remoulded letters
something plastic is malleable, so the letters are remoulded

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A shopper wanting each item wrapped in less plastic packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' looks like packaging; here it means malleable, rearranging LESS to SLES around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Discount events in shops are where goods at reduced prices, the answer to 10, are offered.

clue.text: Power lies with Europe manoeuvring around as it's hard to see through

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: the rearranged continent goes around the two-letter word
the word manoeuvres into a new order

explanation.surface: Power politics in Europe, all manoeuvring and murk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manoeuvring' gives EOUPER, and 'around' puts AS after its first E.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick yellowish smog, as in old London, through which visibility is poor.

clue.text: Wobbly bodies seen in these?

parts.note: a swimming head feels unsteady and wobbly
trunks are torsos, the main body

explanation.surface: A wry glance at flabby physiques on show at the beach or pool.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: swimwear in which flabby bodies are on display.
explanation.definitionFit: Men's shorts worn for bathing, which show off the wearer's physique.
